title: Ambassadors drawn out by jazz concerts
summary: At embassies, diplomats who ignored invitations came to hear Benny Carter's band, and the group was received warmly abroad.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And another thing that was good about it, you had the time.
See, because if you'd been -- like, I mean, when Duke went through there, they were mostly playing nearly everyday.

See, we wouldn't play but an hour a night, you know. And every day, we'd have dinner with the ambassador and his family and in -- let's see, in one place there, the ambassador, American ambassador, he had been trying to get a rendezvous with most of the political figures there -- I think it was in Amman. Amman or Damascus. It must have been Damascus. And they had a big party for the band and -- in his home there, the ambassador's home -- and they had a luncheon and he was so -- he wrote -- he sent all the invitations to like the Communist ambassador and all of them, you know, and they all showed up and he had never heard of Benny Carter, the ambassador from America, but the other ambassadors had heard of Benny Carter.
Isn't that something? 'Isn't it amazing? And he told Benny, he says, you know, he had been trying just to get to speak to these political figures ever since he'd been ambassador.
This is how he got it.
Now jazz brings them to the concert.
And yet they won't really give it credit.
They won't give it credit. Amazing, it's amazing.
It's amazing. Just as soon as we got off the plane, people started talking about Louie Armstrong.

And Pearl Bailey, she's quite a favorite in Jordan. She's very -- she was a good queen -- good friend of Queen Alia and King Hussein too because she's performed over there. And then we went to another place -- I can't remember where it was -- but this ambassador had been trying to give a luncheon for all the diplomats. Nobody -- they would just ignore the invitation, you know, and he gave a luncheon and he expected none of them to come, you know. All of them came.
And he was -- like we had a fellow there that was really responsible for us going. His name is Dr. Morroe Berger.
